sender.en: “Public Security Bureau”, Chinese or Hong Kong police, or anti-corruption officials

name.en: Fake Chinese police call: “you are under investigation, pay or be arrested”

how.en: Callers pretending to be police from China or Hong Kong, such as the Public Security Bureau, tell members of the Asian community in Canada, often students, that they are involved in a crime. They know some personal details to seem real, demand secrecy and threaten arrest or deportation. Victims are pressured to transfer money, travel, or buy gold and hand it to people posing as officers.

text.en: A caller says they are police from China or Hong Kong and accuses you of a crime.
They say you must cooperate now or face arrest or deportation.
They tell you not to tell family or friends.
They ask you to transfer money, or convert savings into gold and hand it to an “officer”.
This is the Public Security Bureau. Your identity has been used in a money laundering case. You must cooperate with our investigation. Do not tell anyone, or you will be arrested.

en: accused of money laundering in china
told to buy gold for the police
threatened with deportation on the phone
hong kong police said i'm under investigation
An unexpected call from foreign police accusing you of a crime.
Being told to keep it secret from family and friends.
Threats of arrest or deportation if you don’t act now.
Being told to travel, withdraw money or buy gold.
Hang up. Police never demand money, gold or valuables as part of an investigation.
Talk to a trusted friend or family member before doing anything.
Report threats to your local police and to the Canadian Anti-Fraud Centre.

sources.title: Extortion targeting Asian communities – law enforcement impersonation
